cards.explanation: The advice David is hearing is, “Flee like a bird to your mountain!” David has just said he takes refuge in the LORD, and then he asks how anyone can say that to him (Psalm 11:1). It's like telling someone who's already home to go look for a house. Pack up, fly off, find a mountain. David isn't taking that advice.

The wicked are aiming at the upright in heart. They set their arrow on the string “…to shoot from the shadows at the upright in heart” (Psalm 11:2). They're lining up the shot from the shadows, friends, and I think that's a sneaky way to go about it. David puts it plainly in verse 2.

The answer is the foundations. The question goes, “If the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do?” (Psalm 11:3). A foundation is what everything else sits on. When I'm pressing cookies, if the counter wobbles, nothing else matters. That's why this question lands so hard.

David says the LORD is in His holy temple. He says, “The LORD is in His holy temple; the LORD is on His heavenly throne” (Psalm 11:4). The advice had a mountain in it, and David's answer starts with where the LORD is. David is looking at the LORD, friends, not at the escape route.

The answer is True. David says, “His eyes are watching closely; they examine the sons of men” (Psalm 11:4). That comes right after he says the LORD is on His heavenly throne. Watching closely and examining, that's what the verse says.

The answer is False. David says, “The LORD tests the righteous and the wicked…” (Psalm 11:5). Both groups, not just one. I'd honestly rather be on the tested list than ignored, because being tested means He's paying attention.

The answer is the lover of violence. David says, “His soul hates the lover of violence” (Psalm 11:5). This one is heavy, friends, and I think it hurts to read it slowly. David says it straight, and I'm going to leave it that way.

The answer is fiery coals and sulfur. David says, “On the wicked He will rain down fiery coals and sulfur; a scorching wind will be their portion” (Psalm 11:6). This is a heavy verse, so I'll just let it sit. The psalm says it, and David says it plainly.

The answer is justice. David says, “For the LORD is righteous; He loves justice” (Psalm 11:7). Righteous and loving justice go together. It's good news, bakers, when the One on the throne cares about what's right.

The answer is that the upright will see His face. David ends the psalm with, “The upright will see His face” (Psalm 11:7). After the arrows, the shadows and the heavy verses, this is how it closes. I think that's a good place to land, friends.
